notes:
1. Title and dek: "Banks open the door to AI inside, and keep it shut outside". Only JPMorgan is sourced as blocking outside agents; the Wells Fargo and DBS sources say nothing about outside agents. Fix: narrow the title to what the sources show, e.g. "JPMorgan keeps outside AI agents out while Wells Fargo and DBS use them inside".
2. Section 4 says "We can read the same pattern across the three banks: wide use of AI on the inside, with people keeping the final call." Only the DBS source says humans make the approval decisions ("bankers and credit risk managers still make the assessment and approval decisions"). The Wells Fargo source says only "a disciplined approach to managing risk", and the JPMorgan section says nothing about internal use or human sign-off. Fix: drop the three-bank pattern sentence, or limit it to DBS; retitle "Humans still sign off" so it does not cover all three (e.g. "At DBS, humans still sign off").
3. Section 3 says Wells Fargo chairman and CEO Charlie Scharf "said the bank is using AI and, in some cases, autonomous agents to write code faster...". Source (PYMNTS, own voice): "The bank is using AI and, in some cases, autonomous agents to write code faster, launch marketing campaigns faster, close previously unknown cyber vulnerabilities..."; Scharf is quoted only on "We're excited by the opportunities AI presents... taking a disciplined approach to managing risk". Fix: "Wells Fargo is using AI and, in some cases, autonomous agents to ..., PYMNTS reported, and Scharf said the bank is taking a disciplined approach to managing risk."
4. Section 3 heading "Inside the bank, agents already work" covers two banks and says agents work at both. Wells Fargo uses autonomous agents "in some cases"; DBS's agentic tool is described as "the newer effort". Fix: "Inside the banks, AI is already at work" or similar.
5. Section 5 says Harbor "also says insurers do not have the claims history to price the risk of AI agents." Source (Insurance Journal, own voice): "When it comes to AI agents, insurers do not have the claims history to price the risk. So some insurers are excluding AI out of existing policies, Harbor said." Only the second sentence is credited to Harbor. Fix: "Insurance Journal reports that insurers do not have the claims history to price the risk of AI agents." Same wording issue in the Harbor brief body ("Harbor also says insurers do not have the claims history to price AI agent risk"): change to "Insurance Journal reports insurers do not have...".
6. Section 2 opens "Meanwhile the door is not fully shut". "Meanwhile" adds a time link the source does not give and the door sentence is the writer's gloss. Fix: "Agents can still see some customer data in a read-only way..., CNBC reports, but they can't send money or pay a bill."
7. Brief 2026-10-14-jpmorgan-outside-agents-accounts, body: "Agents can still read some data, such as balances, through connectors like Plaid." Source: "AI agents can access some customer data from Chase accounts in a read-only fashion, such as customer balances, if Plaid or another connector has the user's credentials." Fix: add the condition: "...through connectors like Plaid, if the connector has the user's credentials." Also body says "citing risk to clients"; source: "citing risks to the company and its customers" / "too risky for clients and for JPMorgan". Fix: "citing risk to clients and the bank".
